problemType: Students don't use appropriate academic language for different science purposes

Provide function-specific sentence stems (UDL 5.3)
Model function use with think-aloud (UDL 6.1)
Create authentic audiences for academic science communication (UDL 7.2)
studentTasks: Identify the function needed for the communication task
Select appropriate language structures for that function
Use function-specific vocabulary and sentence patterns
Evaluate own writing for appropriate function use
Revise to strengthen function language
supports: Language function reference guide with examples (UDL 3.3)
Model texts demonstrating each function (HLP Exemplars)
Peer editing for function language (HLP Cooperative Learning)
fadePlan: Phase 1: Single function with full sentence stems → Phase 2: Multiple functions with stem bank → Phase 3: Function selection without stems → Phase 4: Natural academic register use
whenNotToUse: During informal discussion or brainstorming where everyday language is appropriate.
formativeChecks: - Function identification accuracy
- Language structure use in writing
- Self and peer evaluation quality
- Register appropriateness for audience

subject: science
name: Collaborative Sense-Making Discussion Protocol
problemType: Students share answers but don't build on each other's scientific reasoning
targetMisconception: Belief that classroom discussion is about giving correct answers rather than constructing understanding together
teacherMoves: Establish talk moves that require building on others: 'I want to add to what ___ said...' 'I respectfully disagree because...' (HLP Cooperative Learning)
Use strategic pausing after student contributions to invite building (wait time 2.0 - after student response)
Revoice student contributions to model academic science language while honoring original idea (UDL 2.1 - clarifying vocabulary)
Track idea development visibly on board showing how class thinking evolved (UDL 3.3 - information display)
Explicitly teach: 'In science, we build theories together - no single person has all the answers' (UDL 7.2 - disciplinary norms)
studentTasks: Listen actively to peer contributions (documented with listening notes)
Build on, question, or respectfully challenge peer ideas using accountable talk stems
Contribute own reasoning with evidence to class theory-building
Synthesize multiple perspectives into more complete explanation
Reflect on how own thinking changed through discussion
supports: Accountable Talk Moves reference card with sentence stems (UDL 5.3)
Active Listening Note-catcher with 'They said... I'm thinking...' format (UDL 3.3)
Discussion Contribution Tracker (self-assessment of talk move use) (UDL 6.4)
Idea Evolution poster documenting class sense-making journey (visible thinking record) (UDL 3.2)
Small group discussion roles: Questioner, Builder, Synthesizer, Includer (HLP Cooperative Learning)
fadePlan: Phase 1: Teacher facilitates with heavy use of talk moves, explicitly naming each move being used → Phase 2: Students use talk move cards as prompts; teacher continues revoicing → Phase 3: Student discussion leaders facilitate with teacher observation → Phase 4: Natural scientific discourse without explicit prompts; teacher participates as co-learner
whenNotToUse: When students need direct instruction on new content (sense-making requires something to make sense of). Also avoid when only one student has relevant knowledge - can become performance rather than collaborative construction.
formativeChecks: - Tally of building talk moves vs. isolated answer-giving (track ratio over time)
- Observation: Are more students participating? Are same students always building on same people? (equity check)
- Exit reflection: 'One idea from a classmate that changed my thinking was...'
- Discussion transcript analysis for evidence of genuine idea development vs. parallel monologues

whenNotToUse: When addressing phenomena that could exploit or sensationalize community struggles without genuine partnership. Also avoid when time constraints prevent meaningful community engagement - better to do fewer phenomena deeply than many superficially.
formativeChecks: - Quality of community connections in student writing (specific family/neighborhood references)
- Observation of student engagement during notice/wonder (increased participation from historically marginalized students = success)
- Parent/family feedback on relevance of investigations
- Student exit tickets: 'Why does this investigation matter to people in our community?'

Practice evaluating measurement quality in real data (UDL 6.3)
Connect to real-world consequences of measurement error (UDL 7.2)

Identify sources of measurement error in procedures
Report measurements with appropriate significant figures
Evaluate data quality and discuss limitations
Design procedures to improve precision or accuracy

Error source identification guide by measurement type (UDL 6.2)
fadePlan: Phase 1: Teacher identifies error sources and evaluates data quality → Phase 2: Guided identification with prompts → Phase 3: Independent analysis with self-check → Phase 4: Design investigations prioritizing measurement quality
whenNotToUse: During initial measurement skill development. Focus on technique before adding analysis layer.
formativeChecks: - Concept check: Sort examples into precise/accurate categories
- Error identification in lab procedures

- Reflection: How could we improve our data quality?

subject: science
name: Productive Failure and Mistake Analysis Protocol
problemType: Students give up quickly when experiments fail or produce unexpected results
targetMisconception: Belief that failed experiments indicate personal inadequacy or wasted time rather than valuable learning opportunities
teacherMoves: Explicitly teach the difference between 'failing forward' and giving up using scientist stories from diverse backgrounds (UDL 7.3 - affirming identity)

studentTasks: Document unexpected results with same rigor as expected results using structured failure report
Analyze: What did we learn from what didn't work? (specific evidence required)
Generate hypotheses for why results differed from predictions
Design follow-up investigation based on failure analysis
Share failure-to-learning stories in brief presentations
supports: Failure Report Template with sections: What I expected / What happened / What I learned / What I'd try next (UDL 3.3)

whenNotToUse: When students are in acute distress or when the failure stems from safety violations that need immediate correction rather than analysis. Also avoid during high-stakes assessments where failure analysis could increase anxiety.
formativeChecks: - Observe student response to unexpected results: Do they persist or shut down? Track change over time
- Collect failure reports and analyze for depth of 'what I learned' section
- Student self-rating of frustration tolerance before/after unit
- Count of 'I'm stuck' help-seeking (increase = positive - shows safety to admit confusion)

subject: science

Show all work with units and scientific meaning annotations
Interpret numerical answer in context of phenomenon
Evaluate whether answer makes sense given scientific understanding
Communicate quantitative findings with appropriate precision

Error analysis protocol for incorrect calculations (HLP Explicit Instruction)
fadePlan: Phase 1: Full worked examples with explicit meaning annotations → Phase 2: Partial examples with meaning prompts → Phase 3: Independent calculation with interpretation requirement → Phase 4: Student-generated problems with solutions
whenNotToUse: During conceptual introduction before quantitative relationships are established. Also avoid when math anxiety requires additional SEL support first.
formativeChecks: - Compare estimates to calculations: Are they in same order of magnitude?
- Check interpretation statements for scientific accuracy
- Observe: Do students catch unreasonable answers before submitting?
- Exit ticket: Calculate and explain what the number means scientifically

subject: science

- Growth tracking: How has reflection changed over time?

subject: science

Share how science knowledge is used in diverse careers and contexts (UDL 7.3)

- Peer sharing participation and quality
- Ongoing relevance journal entries

subject: science

- Evaluate analogy quality: Is the comparison accurate and helpful?

subject: science
name: Science Anxiety Recognition and Management
problemType: Students experience anxiety that interferes with science learning and performance

Reflect on anxiety management growth

- Reflection on strategy effectiveness

subject: science

Identify careers that match personal interests and values
Research pathways including education and experience needed
Connect with professionals in fields of interest
Create preliminary career exploration plan
supports: Career exploration guide organized by science field (UDL 3.3)
fadePlan: Phase 1: Teacher provides career information and connections → Phase 2: Guided exploration with resources → Phase 3: Independent exploration with mentorship connections → Phase 4: Ongoing career development as part of identity
whenNotToUse: When students are in crisis and basic needs must be addressed first. Return to career exploration when appropriate.
formativeChecks: - Career exploration breadth: how many options considered?
- Pathway plan realism: are steps achievable?
- Connection follow-through: are informational interviews happening?
- Reflection on career interest evolution

subject: science
name: Building Science Discourse Community

teacherMoves: Establish discourse norms that require building (UDL 8.3)

Talk move cards for student desks (UDL 5.3)
Idea tracker display for building understanding (UDL 3.3)

formativeChecks: - Track discourse moves: building or parallel?
- Observe: Does idea tracker show development?
- Participation equity patterns
- Reflection on collective vs individual learning

subject: science

teacherMoves: Display diverse scientists including those with disabilities and from all backgrounds (UDL 7.3)

Celebrate diverse ways of doing science (UDL 7.1)

Document contributions to science in this class

supports: Diverse scientist biography bank organized by identity and field (UDL 7.3)
Science in My Life' connection map (UDL 7.2)
Contribution tracker for class science work (UDL 6.4)
fadePlan: Phase 1: Teacher provides identity connections and diverse examples → Phase 2: Students explore connections with guided resources → Phase 3: Students identify own connections with peer sharing → Phase 4: Students mentor others in science identity development
whenNotToUse: Never - all students benefit from science identity affirmation. Adapt activities to student needs and comfort levels.
formativeChecks: - Track identity language use in writing and speech
- Observe engagement changes over time
- Reflection quality on identity prompts
- Peer and self-identification as scientists

subject: science

Present findings with action recommendations

formativeChecks: Community presentation feedback
Action plan feasibility check

subject: science
name: Science Note-Taking Strategy System

- Reflection on strategy effectiveness

subject: science

whenNotToUse: When text is far above reading level without modifications. Provide accessible versions or read-alouds for differentiation.
formativeChecks: - Check annotations for evidence of active meaning-making
- Evaluate summaries for accuracy and completeness
- Observe: Do students use previewing strategies independently?
- Exit ticket: 'What was the main finding and one question you still have?'

subject: science

formativeChecks: - Planning document quality
- Draft to revision changes (substantive or surface?)
- Peer feedback quality
- Final writing quality relative to draft

subject: science

whenNotToUse: During initial content learning when students need to build foundational knowledge before evaluating claims. Also avoid with topics that may cause undue distress without appropriate support (e.g., climate anxiety requires SEL scaffolding).

- Quality of 'citizen response' writing: Does it reference evidence quality and limitations?
- Self-reported confidence in evaluating scientific claims in daily life
- Observation: Do students spontaneously apply framework to current events discussions?

subject: science
